question_interpretation: Whether Wazir's pre-1929 permanent lease binds the claimant mortgagee through the earlier Bank security, accounting for parties, dates, prior decisions and live appeal scope.
allowed_answer_boundary: Retrospective source-only reconstruction from all 18 CASE and 23 LAW entries. Prior judgments attributed; target court reasoning and result withheld. Public excerpts only, no exhibits or outside law.

items.criterion: Assess whether Wazir could grant a 1925 permanent lease binding the plaintiff through the earlier mortgage; the later appellate issue concerns power before section 65-A (1929).
mandatory_constraints: Issue only; ultimate holding withheld.

evidence.quote: the only question which survived for our consideration was whether Wazir Narayan Singh had the power to grant a permanent lease to the defendants so as to bind the plaintiff.

items.criterion: Raja Nilkanth owned Gadi Sirampur and mortgaged it to Chota Nagpur Banking Association on 1 August 1914.
mandatory_constraints: Raja is original mortgagor; Bank is earlier mortgagee.

evidence.quote: he executed the 1st August, 1914, a simple mortgage of Gadi Sirampur in favour of the Chota Nagpur Banking Association Limited.

items.criterion: The Bank sued Wazir in 1920, obtained a 1921 decree, purchased only a one-third share in 1922, and that sale was challenged.
mandatory_constraints: Bank execution distinct from plaintiff's 1935 purchase.

evidence.quote: The Bank purchased a third share of Gadi Sirampur in execution of that decree the 28th October, 1922.

items.criterion: On 5 November 1925 Wazir granted a registered permanent Patta over Nawadih, Koldih, Pandna and Chihutia to Hiraman and his son Chohan.
mandatory_constraints: Four villages, not the whole estate; after 1914, before 1926.

evidence.quote: Wazir Narain Singh granted a permanent lease of four villages Nawadih, Koldih, Pandna and Chihutia by a registered Patta

items.criterion: To satisfy the Bank, Wazir mortgaged Gadi Sirampur on 14 August 1926 to the plaintiff estate's Court of Wards manager for Rs. 1,47,000; Bank dues were paid and its sale set aside.
mandatory_constraints: Separate later mortgage; setting aside the Bank sale did not itself cancel the Patta.

evidence.quote: to secure repayment of a sum of Rs. 1,47,000 and out of the same satisfied the dues of the Bank and the sale in favour of the Ban was accordingly set aside.

items.criterion: The plaintiff filed the 1929 mortgage-enforcement suit, naming Hiraman as defendant 20 and Hiraman's father Dilo as defendant 19, while Chohan was not named there.
mandatory_constraints: Keep roles separate from 1939 defendants; lack of joinder was contested.

evidence.quote: Hiraman Ram as defendant 20 and his father Dilo Ram as defendant 19.

items.criterion: The plaintiff obtained the final sale decree in 1931, bought Gadi Sirampur in April 1935, and received court delivery in February 1936.
mandatory_constraints: Not the Bank's 1922 purchase; delivery does not negate lessees' continued occupation.

evidence.quote: Plaintiff purchased Gadi Sirampur at the auction sale held in execution of this decree the 6th April, 1935.

items.criterion: Hiraman and Chohan continued physically possessing the disputed villages; plaintiff sued them for khas possession in November 1939.
mandatory_constraints: Dilo had died; 1939 suit differs from 1929 mortgage suit.

evidence.quote: Hiraman Ram and his son Chohan Ram continued in actual possession of the disputed villages

items.criterion: Plaintiff argued subrogation, binding mortgage decree, execution purchase, and resulting extinguishment of the Patta.
mandatory_constraints: Attribute as pleading; claim that Patta postdated plaintiff mortgage conflicts with 1925/1926 dates.
items.importance_reason: States claimant's route without adopting it.

evidence.quote: The plaintiff contended that he was subrogated to the position of the Bank

items.criterion: Chohan denied plaintiff's subrogation and decree's binding effect because he was not personally a mortgage-suit party; he said the auction could not end the Patta.
mandatory_constraints: Chohan's arguments, superseded in part by later unchallenged findings.

evidence.quote: He contended that the decree in the mortgage suit was not binding him as he was not :a party to that suit.

items.criterion: Hiraman denied being family manager/karta and alleged a later family partition allotting the villages to Chohan.
mandatory_constraints: Allegations, not established partition or ownership.

evidence.quote: the properties had been allotted at that partition to the defendant 2.

items.criterion: Trial court found Hiraman the Hindu-family manager/karta, Chohan represented, and the mortgage decree binding the defendants.
mandatory_constraints: Attribute to trial court; distinguish contested pleas.

evidence.quote: the defendant 1 was the Manager and Karta of the joint family and that the defendant 2 was fully represented in the mortgage suit

items.criterion: Trial court awarded plaintiff possession and mesne profits; defendants appealed.
mandatory_constraints: Superseded by contrary High Court result; no target-court endorsement.

evidence.quote: the plaintiff was entitled to recover possession 112 of the said properties and mesne profits from the defendants.

items.criterion: Patna High Court rejected plaintiff's constructive-res-judicata argument.
mandatory_constraints: Rejection is distinct from sufficient representation; do not reverse outcome.

evidence.quote: The High Court negatived the contention in regard to constructive res judicata

items.criterion: Patna High Court used section 66 and treated whether the lease made the Bank security insufficient as crucial to Wazir's power.
mandatory_constraints: Historical High Court approach, not target holding or full statutory formulation.

evidence.quote: the crucial test was whether the lease rendered the mortgagee's security insufficient.

items.criterion: Although plaint did not allege insufficiency, High Court calculated figures and found the Patta did not render Bank security insufficient.
mandatory_constraints: Attributed numerical finding only; calculations absent.

evidence.quote: there was no allegation in the plaint that the defendant's lease had the effect of rendering the security of -the Bank insufficient

items.criterion: High Court held lease valid and unaffected by plaintiff mortgage, decree or auction; dismissed possession suit. Plaintiff appealed further.
mandatory_constraints: High Court result, not withheld target disposition.

evidence.quote: It therefore held that the lease was valid and was not affected by the plaintiff's mortgage, decree or by the execution sale under that decree

items.criterion: Both lower courts found plaintiff subrogated to the Bank; this finding was expressly unchallenged in later appeal.
mandatory_constraints: Finding not fresh target reasoning; Bank rights predate Patta.

evidence.quote: Both the Courts below found that the plaintiff was subrogated to the position of the Bank.

items.criterion: Both lower courts found Chohan sufficiently represented in mortgage proceedings; this was expressly unchallenged later.
mandatory_constraints: Does not mean Chohan was personally named in 1929.

evidence.quote: They also found that the defendant 2 was sufficiently represented in the mortgage suit. These findings were not challenged before us

items.criterion: Section 65-A's regulated leasing power was inserted in 1929, after the 1925 Patta; its conditions cannot be assumed retroactively decisive.
mandatory_constraints: Do not infer permanent leases automatically invalid; deed variations and time applicability unproved.

evidence.quote: 28 Ins. by Act 20 of 1929, sec. 30.30

items.criterion: Section 66 addresses destructive or permanently injurious acts when mortgage security is/will become insufficient, with specified one-third coverage (one-half for buildings); assess High Court shorthand against that text.
mandatory_constraints: Insufficiency alone does not state every element; no original figures given.
items.importance_reason: Tests the lower court's legal premise.

evidence.quote:
he must not commit any act which is destructive
or permanently injurious thereto, if the security is insufficient or will be rendered insufficient
by such act.

items.criterion: If Wazir's grant bound the prior Bank mortgage, plaintiff's derived title/auction does not alone extinguish it; if not, possession relief may follow subject to other applicable rules.
mandatory_constraints: Conditional alternative paths only; section 111(c) or other lease-termination grounds require proved predicates.

evidence.quote: whether Wazir Narayan Singh had the power to grant a permanent lease to the defendants so as to bind the plaintiff.
